p1: There's a reason the mall on Route 9 pays its night guard double.
I found out on my first shift.
Taped inside the security booth was a card. Five rules. Handwritten.
Rule one. Do your rounds at midnight, two, and four. Never at three.
Rule two. If the escalators start on their own, don't ride them.
Rule three. The eleven mannequins in Halbrook's face the window. Always.
If one is facing you, don't turn your back on it.
I laughed. The old guard didn't.
He just said, rule five is the one that matters.
Rule five had been scratched out.
At two fifty-eight, camera four showed me something I still can't explain.
Every mannequin in Halbrook's... was facing my booth.
Part two is next. Follow, so you're not alone for it.
p2: Every mannequin in Halbrook's was facing my booth.
Rule three said don't turn your back. So I didn't.
I watched camera four for eleven minutes. Nothing moved.
Then my radio clicked on. Static... then breathing.
Then the escalators started. All of them. At three a.m.
And something was riding one up.
Slowly. Toward the second floor. Toward me.
I checked camera four again. One of the mannequins was gone.
I grabbed the rule card and held it to the light.
Under the scratches, I could just make out rule five.
Part three is the last one. Follow. You need to hear how this ends.
p3: Rule five. Two words, scratched out so I wouldn't read them.
The card said Halbrook's has eleven mannequins.
I counted the window on camera four.
The escalators stopped. The radio went dead.
And right behind me... the booth door clicked shut.
I didn't turn around. Rule three. I stared at that screen until sunrise.
At six twelve, I finally turned. The booth was empty.
Camera four showed eleven mannequins again.
Last week, I drove past the mall. They're hiring a night guard again.
